perf-bot: Nightly perf alert: 00:12 UTC window shows +85% p99 latency and -30% throughput for v2-serving across eu-west-1. Alerting rule: nightly-slo-drift. Suspected correlated spike at 00:07 after recent canary merge. :warning:

alex: saw the alert, digging in. which canary? link?

mike: grafana: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/serving/nightly?panel=kv-miss-rate -> kv miss rate jumped from 4% -> 22% at 00:07, batch size distribution tightened (more small batches).

jen: I ran `runtest_perf --profile --region eu-west-1 --since 00:00` and repro shows tail latencies up. Quick flame: kernel-selection time increased, more fallbacks to `generic_kernel` for attentions.

sara: that matches a merge from earlier today (commit 0a7d4f3) that reworked op ordering in fused attention to improve memory reuse. hypothesis: new schedule broke our kernel prober heuristics so prober prefers fallback path and batching stalls.

alex: can we bisect? I kicked off `git bisect` on the release branch with the nightly harness. so far candidate commit is 0a7d4f3 -> changes in scheduler heuristics.

mike: CI perf run for that PR did show a tiny regression in microbench (0.6% median) but not flagged. CI note: `ci/perf-nightly` failed on the branch build at 00:05 with increased kv miss. logs: ```
[00:05:12] kv_cache: miss_rate=0.21
[00:05:12] kernel_prober: fallback_count=345
[00:05:12] batcher: avg_batch=2.1 -> expected 4.8
```

jen: repro profile attached (short): `time_in_kernel_selector: +120ms`, `op_order_adjust: 0.8ms` — selector is calling a more expensive probe per request now.

alex: workaround idea: pin prober epsilon to previous threshold (0.03 -> 0.01) to avoid expensive probes. quick A/B rollout?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout for release/v2 started at 23:50 UTC. Current canary at 15% hosts. Pause reason: manual pause by jen (rollout-blocker).

sara: we can either revert 0a7d4f3 or patch scheduler to preserve the kernel_probe short-circuit. revert is fastest for rollback.

mike: +1 to revert on canary and run another nightdash pass. If revert fixes kv miss and batch sizes normalize, promote.

jen: I'll open a revert PR now and add `ci/perf-nightly` as required for the follow-up. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4789 (revert 0a7d4f3)

alex: after revert goes to canary, we'll run the same perf harness and compare: `runtest_perf --compare baseline:1768790000 --candidate:canary-4789 --profiles=kernel_selector,kv_cache,batcher`

mike: assigning follow-ups: alex -> perf compare + diff dashboards; jen -> revert PR and canary rollout; sara -> quick patch idea if revert not clean. tagging oncall: @sara @alex @jen. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Noted. Next automated check scheduled in 15m. If p99 > 2x baseline, escalation to paging will happen.
